statement: At high temperatures (k_B*T >> hbar*c/d), the Casimir force between two ideal conducting plates separated by distance d transitions from its zero-temperature quantum form to a classical thermal limit dominated by the zeroth Matsubara frequency. In this high-T regime, identify the functional dependence of the Casimir pressure P on k_B*T and d (ignore all prefactors; give only the functional scaling form).
find: Functional scaling of Casimir pressure P in the high-temperature limit k_B*T >> hbar*c/d (up to a numerical prefactor).
notes: In the Matsubara formalism, thermal corrections appear at frequencies xi_n = 2*pi*n*k_B*T/hbar. When k_B*T >> hbar*c/d, only the n=0 term survives and contributes a pressure P = -zeta(3)*k_B*T/(8*pi*d^3) ~ k_B*T/d^3. This classical limit, first derived by Mehra (1967), is purely thermal and independent of hbar — it persists even for non-ideal conductors. The scaling k_B*T/d^3 contrasts with the zero-T result hbar*c/d^4.
